what: both actors evaluated at the SAME recorded states, so the on-policy state distribution cannot carry the high-risk EDGE contrast; plus a risk-response curve on fixed state sets as an unconfounded replacement for the share metric

confound_being_addressed.where: the Rung 2 headline metric itself, and every high-risk EDGE share quoted since Sprint 6
confound_being_addressed.what: each arm's share is computed on its OWN trajectory; denominators differ (2174 vs 1418 high-risk entries) and episode lengths differ (A0 374.2 with 0/32 truncated; R2 392.1 with 17/32), so a policy difference and a state-distribution difference are not separable
confound_being_addressed.why_it_is_structural: risk is high at a host BECAUSE tasks remain on it; STAY keeps an agent in a high-risk state and MIGRATE_EDGE removes it from one, so conditioning on 'in a high-risk state' selects for 'just chose STAY'. The metric has its own outcome in the denominator.
confound_being_addressed.not_a_computation_error: both figures use the same definition and are reproduced EXACTLY on the diagonal here; the defect is identification, not arithmetic
resolution: cross-evaluate pi_A0 and pi_R2 at identical states, paired within state, clustered by episode
score risk RESPONSE on a fixed state set instead of a share on a policy-dependent one

definition.starts: same construction and seed as _diag_rung2_75_edgeshare_cluster --cell production
definition.random_source: uniform over legal actions; depends on neither arm. CAVEAT: visits states off-manifold for both, so it is a neutral reference, not a realistic one.
definition.union_source: A0's recorded states pooled with R2's, episode ids kept disjoint. Symmetric by construction and fully on-manifold for both arms, at the cost of containing both arms' selection effects rather than none.

not_a_fix: forward passes only; no optimiser, no gradient, no write to any checkpoint; production code unmodified

calibration_of_primary_metric.what: the proposed primary metric (risk response) computed for every arm that ALREADY EXISTS, on the neutral state sets
calibration_of_primary_metric.why: a GO threshold for the next rung has to be set against the spread this metric already shows across completed training runs, otherwise the threshold is invented
calibration_of_primary_metric.no_new_training: A1/A2/A3 are existing Sprint 7 checkpoints scored with forward passes only; they generate no state source, so they cannot shift the state sets

conclusion.metric_as_used_since_sprint6: NOT identified: the paired within-state contrast reverses sign between A0's own state set (+) and R2's own state set (-), so the on-policy high-risk EDGE share does not measure a property of the policy. Both the Rung 2 'win' and the Rung 2.5 'loss' fail as policy-quality claims.
conclusion.direction_on_neutral_sets: on the two state sets that privilege neither arm (uniform-random and pooled), R2's pi(EDGE) at high risk exceeds A0's consistently -- so the confound invalidated the METRIC, not the direction of the policy difference
conclusion.recommended_primary_metric: risk RESPONSE on a FIXED, policy-independent state set: pi(MIGRATE_EDGE | risk>=0.6) - pi(MIGRATE_EDGE | risk<0.2), plus Spearman(risk, pi(EDGE)) over decision entries. No policy appears in the state distribution, so the quantity is identified.
